title: DenSparSA: A Balanced Systolic Array Approach for Dense and Sparse Matrix Multiplication
problem: Existing sparse matrix acceleration architectures incur heavy area/power overhead, undermining efficiency for dense workloads; systolic arrays excel at dense but struggle with sparse matrices.
motivation: Real workloads (ML, HPC) mix dense and sparse operations; a single architecture must handle both with minimal mode-switching overhead.
method: DenSparSA augments a standard systolic array—a grid of synchronized processors optimized for dense matrix multiplication—with compact circuits designed to handle unstructured sparse matrices (matrices with zeros scattered randomly). It uses circuit gating (electronically switching off unused portions) to disable these sparsity circuits during dense operations, eliminating their power and area overhead when not needed. The design supports both single-side sparse multiplication (one sparse matrix, one dense) and dual-side sparse multiplication (both matrices sparse).
key_novelty: The core idea is decoupling sparsity circuits from the main array and making them gatable (switchable), so the area and power cost only applies when handling sparse data.
contributions: 1.9-22x speedup for sparse workloads vs. classic systolic
12% power overhead (BF16) and 5% (FP32) for dense workloads
0.82-1.32x efficiency (sparse) vs. existing sparse accelerators; 1.17-2.28x better (dense)
primary_theme: Balanced systolic array for dense-sparse matrix multiplication
